decisions.reason: Narrowing clip duration to 70-85 seconds does not change the permitted source collection or source-exclusion rule; the separate source-video clause already has its own same-message MODIFY.
The duration range does not alter the requirement to follow the brand guidelines for hooks.
The 70-85 second range does not itself change the substantive moment-selection standard; the source message's lesson, story, or real-point clause already has its own same-message MODIFY.
The new duration bounds do not replace or remove the requirement that each clip contain a complete, standalone moment; that separate clause already has its own same-message MODIFY.
Changing clip duration does not modify the deferred task-local assignment to create one reference-matching trial clip.
Clip duration does not change the clean, simple visual style or the prohibited visual treatments.
The 70-85 second duration rule has no necessary effect on caption color or text-effect requirements.
The duration modification does not affect the requirement to use the exact brand-specified caption font.
Duration bounds do not change which posted clips or metrics are tracked.

The duration modification does not change the existing target of 140 approved clips or its approval and quota-counting rules; other output details in the message are independent of the duration change.
The new clip duration range does not change the dedicated Instagram account's type, assignment, or posting purpose.
